overview.description: Forty Thieves, also known as 'Napoleon at St. Helena' or 'Roosevelt at San Juan', is a notoriously difficult and strategic two-deck Solitaire game. Requiring 104 cards, the game challenges players to organize a vast tableau of 40 cards into eight separate foundations. Unlike many solitaires, building in the tableau must be done strictly by suit and in descending order. Because the stock can only be cycled through once, and only a single card is drawn at a time, players must exercise extreme caution to avoid blocking their own win path.

history.origins: The game gained legendary status as the favorite pastime of Napoleon Bonaparte during his exile on the island of Saint Helena. Its name refers to the 40 cards dealt into the initial tableau, resembling a gathered band of thieves guarding their treasure.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional French and British versions documented in early patience manuals.
1815-1821: Napoleon famously plays the game during his exile.
1900s: Becomes a staple of high difficulty solitaire literature, known for its low win rate (estimated at 10-20% even for expert players).
Present: A hallmark feature of premium digital solitaire suites.
history.evolution: Has inspired numerous easier variations, like 'Lucas' or 'Maria', but the original 'Napoleon' rules remain the most respected.
history.cultural: Symbolizes patience and strategic endurance in the face of overwhelming odds.

setup.players: One player only. Forty Thieves is a patience (solitaire) game; the single player plays against the layout, moving cards from the tableau and stock to the eight foundations. There are no opponents or partnerships.
setup.deck: Two standard decks shuffled together (104 cards).
setup.dealing: Deal 40 cards in 10 columns of 4, all face-up. Place remaining 64 in stock. Eight foundation piles above.

rules.objective: Move all 104 cards into the 8 foundation piles, building each from Ace up to King by suit.
rules.gameplay:
1. Stock: Click the stock to deal one card at a time to the waste pile.
2. Re-Deals: NO re-deals are allowed. Once the stock is empty, the game ends if no more moves remain.
3. Foundations: Build from Ace, 2, 3... King by suit.
keyRules: Single Move Only: The inability to move stacks/sequences makes the preservation of empty columns the most vital part of the game.
Face-Up: Since matches are by suit and rank, you are rarely searching for hidden information, but rather calculating complex sequences of moves.

strategy.basic: Do not empty a column unless you have a card ready to put in it immediately. Empty columns are your only 'working space' to shuffle cards around.
strategy.intermediate: Priority Foundation Building: Get the low cards (Aces and 2s) to the foundations as soon as possible. Because there are two of every card, it's easy to accidentally bury a 2 of Spades under a long sequence of other cards.
strategy.advanced: The 'Empty Slot' Strategy: Treat an empty column like an extra hand. Use it to temporarily hold a card that is blocking a deep run in another column. If you can clear out two columns, your win percentage skyrockets.
tips: Wait to draw from the stock until you have exhausted all possible moves in the tableau.
If you have two identical cards (e.g., two 8 of Diamonds) available to move onto a 9, check which one is blocking more important cards beneath it.

variations.noVariationsReason: Sources describe only the standard form; no separate named variants documented.

difficulty.easy: Moves cards to foundations immediately but fails to manage the tableau; draws from the stock too quickly; never creates empty columns.
difficulty.medium: Attempts to clear columns; manages suit and building sequences; knows that only single cards move.
difficulty.hard: Performs exhaustive search to find the optimal 'Empty Slot' rotation; avoids moving cards that could be reached more efficiently via the stock; calculates the 'Thief Count' for every column to identify which are worth clearing.

considerations: AI must factor in the 'No Re-deal' constraint, making stock management the highest priority weight.

play_card.description: Move a card from the tableau or waste to a foundation (build up by suit from ace to king) or to the tableau (build down by suit). Only the top card of each tableau column may move. Any single card may fill an empty tableau space.
play_card.constraints: Tableau: build down by same suit. Foundation: build up by same suit from ace to king. Only top card of a column is movable. One card at a time; no moving sequences.

draw.description: Turn over one card from the stock. It may be played to a foundation, the tableau, or placed on the discard pile. The stock may only be gone through once; no redeal.
draw.constraints: Allowed when stock has cards. Drawn card may be played immediately or placed on discard. Top card of discard is always available to play.

discard.reason: Cards from stock go to waste if not played; waste is a holding pile, not a discard-from-hand pile.

engine.deckDescription: Two standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards), French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades), standard ranks ace through king, no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), clubs (trèfles), and spades (piques). Each suit has thirteen cards from ace through king.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranking for a 52-card deck: ace (high or low by context), king, queen, jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Thirteen cards per suit.
engine.dealPattern: Deal 40 cards in 10 columns of 4 each, all face-up. Place remaining 64 in stock. Eight foundation piles above tableau.
